messages.content: Hi! I'm going to ask you some questions to build your profile. What are you studying, and what kind of internship are you hoping for?
I'm a sophomore in Information Science with a stats minor. I'd love a data analyst internship next summer, or software engineering if it's backend or web.
Great. Tell me about any work or research you've done so far.
I work at the campus IT help desk and I'm a research assistant in a psychology lab, where I clean survey data in Python and make charts in R.

about_me.answer: I'm a sophomore in Information Science with a Statistics minor at Springfield State. I got into data through my research job: I clean and merge survey data for a psychology lab, about 1,200 participants so far, and I replaced a manual Excel report with R scripts that save the lab around three hours a week. I also work at the IT help desk, which taught me to explain technical things simply. Outside class I built ClassPath, a course-planning app about 150 classmates used. I'm looking for a data analyst internship where I can work on real business questions.

why_field.answer: I like the moment when a messy dataset turns into a clear answer. In the lab, our weekly report used to take three hours of copying numbers into Excel; once I scripted it, the team spent that time discussing results instead. I want a role where that kind of work helps a business decide something, and analytics lets me use both my programming and my statistics.

teamwork.title: Running the club's first Python workshop
teamwork.situation: Our Data Science Club had never run a beginner workshop, and 60 students signed up, far more than the 20 we planned for.
teamwork.task: As treasurer I was asked to make the budget work and help the three officers run it.
teamwork.action: I moved us to a bigger room the department lent for free, split the attendees into tables with one officer each, and wrote a one-page setup guide so we didn't lose the first half hour to installs. I also asked two senior members to float between tables.
teamwork.result: All 60 students finished the first notebook, we stayed $200 under budget, and 14 of them joined the club afterward.
teamwork.reflection: I learned to plan for the problem we'd actually have (installs), not the one on paper, and to ask for help early.

conflict.title: Disagreeing about excluding survey responses
conflict.situation: In the lab, a graduate student wanted to drop every participant who failed one attention check, which would have removed almost 20% of our data.
conflict.task: I was preparing the cleaned dataset and thought the rule was too strict for our study.
conflict.action: Instead of arguing in the meeting, I ran the analysis both ways and showed that results held with a two-check rule while keeping 150 more participants. I brought both versions to our PI and let the data make the case.
conflict.result: The lab adopted the two-check rule and now uses my comparison script for every new study.
conflict.reflection: Showing evidence worked better than debating opinions, and it kept the relationship good.

failure.title: Breaking ClassPath the week before registration
failure.situation: Five days before Fall registration I pushed an update to ClassPath that broke the prerequisite checker for a third of the courses.
failure.task: About 150 classmates were relying on it, and I was the only developer.
failure.action: I rolled back within an hour, posted a note to users, then wrote tests for every prerequisite pattern in the catalog before re-releasing the fix two days later.
failure.result: The fixed version had no further errors through registration.
failure.reflection: I now write tests before changing anything people depend on, and I release small changes instead of big ones.

success.title: Automating the lab's weekly report
success.situation: Our lab built its weekly progress report by copying numbers from several spreadsheets into Excel charts, which took about three hours every week.
success.task: My PI asked if I could make it less painful.
success.action: I wrote R scripts that pull the raw survey exports, apply our cleaning rules and produce the same charts, and documented how to run them.
success.result: The report now takes about 10 minutes, and two other students use the scripts for their own projects.
success.reflection: Small automation can free a whole team's time; I look for repetitive steps first now.

weakness.title: Saying yes to too much
weakness.situation: In my first semester I said yes to every request: extra help desk shifts, club tasks and lab work.
weakness.task: By midterms I was behind in Data Structures.
weakness.action: I started blocking study time on my calendar first, and now I check my week before agreeing to new work and offer a later date when I'm full.
weakness.result: I finished the semester with an A- in Data Structures and kept all three commitments.
weakness.reflection: I still feel the pull to say yes, so I review my calendar every Sunday.

jobs.title: Data Analyst Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.description:
Harborline Logistics (a sample employer for this demo) moves goods for regional retailers. Our analytics team is hiring a Data Analyst Intern for Summer 2027 in Chicago (hybrid, 3 days in office).

What you'll do: build SQL queries and dashboards that track on-time delivery and warehouse throughput; clean shipment data from several systems; present findings to operations managers every two weeks.

What we're looking for: currently pursuing a degree in data science, statistics, information science, business analytics or similar; SQL and Python or R; experience with Tableau or Power BI is a plus; clear communicator. Open to students on F-1 with CPT. Paid: $25/hour.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern (Remote)
jobs.description:
Brightquill Learning (a sample employer for this demo) builds study tools for community colleges. We're hiring remote Software Engineering Interns for Summer 2027.

You'll work on our Python/Flask backend and React front end, write tests, and ship features used by 30,000 students.

Requirements: data structures and one programming language (Python preferred); a project you built and can talk about; comfortable with Git. Nice to have: SQL, JavaScript. Interns are paid $28/hour. We do not sponsor H-1B visas but welcome students with CPT.

jobs.title: Data Science Intern

Northmere Health Analytics (a sample employer for this demo) helps hospitals predict patient no-shows and staffing needs. Summer 2027 Data Science Intern, New York, NY (on-site).

Responsibilities: explore appointment data, build and evaluate simple predictive models (logistic regression, gradient boosting), and write clear summaries for clinical partners.

Qualifications: coursework in statistics and machine learning; Python (pandas, scikit-learn); SQL; interest in healthcare. Must be authorized to work in the US; CPT accepted.
